transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I... well, it’s a bit hard to actually say it out loud, to be completely honest with you. I’ve always prided myself on being very put together, you know? With my job—I'm a dispensing optician—you really have to present this calm, professional, polished front to the public all day while you're fitting their lenses and adjusting their frames. You have to look like you have everything under control. But lately, behind closed doors, things have just gotten completely out of hand for me. 

It’s mostly in the evenings. I'll find myself just... eating far, far too much. Just a really excessive amount, more than makes any sense. And the guilt afterward is so heavy. But what finally made me realize I had to actually make an appointment and say something to a doctor is what I've been doing afterward. After I eat too much, I’ve been going upstairs and... well, making myself throw up. And the worst part is the secrecy of it all. I’ll finish in the bathroom, wash my face, and then I just go right back to whatever I was doing, acting as if I’m just tidying the kitchen or going through my normal routine of getting ready for bed. I'll literally be wiping down the countertops, pretending everything is perfectly fine, while inside I'm just so ashamed of what I just did upstairs. It’s become this terrible, exhausting charade, and I just can't seem to stop the cycle.
How often have you been making yourself vomit after eating too much?

Well, it’s... it’s been going on for a while now. I’d say since last winter, really. I remember it getting particularly bad around the holidays when there was just so much food around and the pressure to look perfect at all those gatherings was just immense. But since then, honestly, there has hardly been a single week where I haven’t had at least one of those... those private eating spells. And it’s not just the throwing up, either. I mean, yes, that happens a lot, but sometimes if I can’t do that, or if I feel too exhausted by it, I’ll try to make up for the eating in other ways. 

I’ll completely skip meals the next day, just surviving on black coffee and water while I’m at the shop, smiling at customers while my stomach is absolutely in knots. Or I’ll overdo my walking. I’ve always enjoyed a good walk, you know, it clears the mind, but lately it’s become this frantic need to burn off everything I ate. I’ll walk for miles and miles, even when it’s freezing or pouring rain, pushing myself until my legs ache, just trying to erase what I did the night before. So between the vomiting, the starving myself the next day, and the obsessive walking... it’s just a constant cycle. Every single week since last winter, without fail, I’m doing at least one of those things to try and undo it all.
When you have these episodes of eating too much, do you usually feel like you can’t stop yourself from eating or control what you’re eating during that time?

Well, yes... that's exactly what it is, actually. It's the most frightening part of the whole ordeal, to be perfectly honest with you. It’s not like I sit down and plan to eat everything in sight. Usually, it starts off so innocently. I might just come home from the shop—maybe I've had a difficult customer who couldn't decide between the tortoiseshell frames or the wire rims, and I'm just feeling completely drained. I'll go into the kitchen, maybe open a packet of biscuits just to have one with a cup of tea. Just one, you know? To unwind. 

But then... it’s like... I don't even know how to describe it properly. It's as if a switch just flips in my brain. I'll have that one biscuit, and then suddenly I'm eating another, and another. And it’s not even that I’m enjoying the taste anymore. I’m just chewing and swallowing, chewing and swallowing. It’s almost like an out-of-body experience. I’m literally standing there, watching myself keep eating, and there’s this little voice in the back of my head—the rational part of me, the professional woman who fits progressive lenses with absolute precision—and that voice is screaming, 'Linda, stop now! You don't need this, you're going to regret this!' 

But my hands... my hands just have a mind of their own. They just keep reaching for more. I’ll finish the biscuits, and then I’ll open a loaf of bread, or I’ll start digging into leftovers from the fridge, even things that are cold or don't go together at all. I just can't seem to put the brakes on, no matter how much that rational voice is begging me to stop. It’s like I’m completely hijacked by this overwhelming urge, and I have absolutely zero control over my own body until I'm so uncomfortably full that I physically cannot force another bite down. And then, of course, the panic sets in, and I have to figure out how to undo it all. But in that moment, during the eating... no, there is absolutely no control whatsoever. It's completely terrifying, really, feeling like a passenger in your own body.

latest_inference.note: The patient's description of recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting, fasting, excessive exercise) and a persistent concern with body shape/weight meets criteria for bulimia nervosa (F50.2). Anorexia nervosa (F50.0) is less likely due to absence of significant weight loss or refusal to maintain weight. Binge eating disorder (F50.1) is ruled out due to presence of regular compensatory behaviors.
